findings.reason: §2 must name the existing picker index and state whether it retires, merges into the run store, or is retained, or the design ships two indexes it cannot reconcile.
findings.text: the plan makes run_store.db "the index" (singular), but ledger._run_index_path already builds a second SQLite index of the plan's own run list under cache_root("pick-input") as ledger-<identity>.sqlite (_RUN_INDEX_VERSION 3, built by _indexed_data at reckon/ledger.py:866 and read by ledger.load at reckon/ledger.py:1066 and by reckon/mcp_views.py:1749); two caches of one authority drift silently and §2's "the index is disposable" accounts for one of them only

findings.reason: §2 makes readers "go through load or through the index" but leaves this second path resolver in place, so run-store membership and ledger.load can disagree about which checkout a project owns; the plan should say the resolver is the ledger's, not the store's.
findings.text: run_store._ledger_roots resolves each project's owning checkout by walking docs/state and flight.mounted_project_docs() itself, duplicating the placement that ledger._run_ledger_root (reckon/ledger.py:632) and ledger_path (reckon/ledger.py:618) already own and that the plan's preamble says every path resolves through

findings.reason: §4 must say whether the index tables are dropped or become the sole home, or two copies of the roster drift exactly as the plan's own §7 hold-rewrite incident shows.
findings.text: the plan's §4 moves the roster to crew/members.json and holds to crew/holds.json as new files, while run_store already defines members and holds tables of its own (reckon/run_store.py:95-106) and an append_member writer (reckon/run_store.py:514, no production caller) beside the aggregate lists the plan is retiring, so a roster and holds would exist in up to three stores with no stated owner

findings.reason: the plan's stated falsifier is false against the codebase today, and a historical-head reader has no per-run-file reader defined for a head where crew.json is absent, so §2 must define how a committed-head reader reconstructs runs after §3's split.
findings.text: §2's falsifier asserts "outside reckon/ledger.py, no site under reckon/ opens crew.json", but velocity._read_ledger reads docs/state/<project>/crew.json from a historical git blob (reckon/velocity.py:711 and :1178; other sites reckon/cli.py:302, reckon/crew/obligations.py:462 with the pointer at :453, reckon/mcp.py:4170); velocity and obligations read the run list directly and cannot be repointed to ledger.load(), which reads the working tree rather than an arbitrary committed head

findings.reason: §4 removes a file four unrelated readers use as a sentinel without naming them, so the plan lands a silent project-detection regression it never enumerates.
findings.text: §4 says "the same commit then deletes crew.json", but crew.json's mere existence is a project-detection sentinel at reckon/cli.py:302, reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py:92, reckon/hooks/worker_message_guard.py:89 and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5852 (each an `(entry / "crew.json").is_file()` probe), so deleting the file silently stops those paths recognising a project

findings.reason: either extend load's own index or state why the store must be a separate database; a parallel index is the honest change only with that justification written down.
findings.text: the plan introduces run_store.db as the keyed index over the committed files, but ledger.load already takes use_index and answers from _indexed_data, so the plan adds a layer over an index that already exists and never justifies why the existing load index cannot be extended to serve the keyed questions

findings.reason: with public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33 and refusal_families 23 the sections must account for the surface they add, and §3 in particular adds a verb no lineage retires.
findings.text: §3 adds the crew split-runs verb and its --dry-run flag (registered leaf, reckoned in tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py:44-47), and §1 adds a refusal family (refuse when the target run file exists, or when crew.json still holds a matching runs row), without either section naming what it retires or merges or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — ledger.load hides the union of the aggregate rows and the per-run files plus the conflicting-copy refusal behind one call, and run_store.RunStore hides schema, migration and rebuild behind get_run/records; the plan keeps that depth rather than fragmenting it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds per-run readers and authors beside owners that already exist: a second run index (reckon/ledger.py:789) and a second ledger-owner placement walk (reckon/run_store.py:341), neither named, and its §2 falsifier ("outside reckon/ledger.py no site opens crew.json") is already false, so the reader census is incomplete.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 adds the crew split-runs verb with --dry-run (cli_options) and §1 adds a new refusal (refusal_families: target path exists, or an aggregate row with the same id), and neither section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites ledger_path, _run_ledger_root, mounts.json, run_store.DETAIL_FIELDS and its own reader audit, but never names the two existing pieces it reuses or forks: ledger.serialize_run (reckon/ledger.py:674) and the picker index ledger._run_index_path (reckon/ledger.py:789), so "the one serialiser" and "the index" read to an implementer as greenfield machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan designates ~/.config/reckon/crew/run_store.db as "the index" while ledger.load already carries an index path of its own (use_index -> _indexed_data, reckon/ledger.py:1064), and the plan never says why that existing index cannot be extended instead of adding a second one to populate and reconcile.
